title: Interest rates (Bank Rate and gilt yields)
headline: Gilts at 5.0% in the OBR's window. A point costs about £13bn by 2029-30.
description: How much higher or lower interest rates are than the OBR assumed in October 2026, sustained across the forecast. Higher rates raise the cost of servicing government debt.

baselinePolicy.text: OBR conditioning assumption, October 2026: Bank Rate averages 4.0% over 2026 and 2027; 10-year gilt yield 5.0% (market prices in the 10 working days to 19 August 2026).

control.formatLabel: percentage points versus the OBR assumption

considerations.text: The forecast's window closed on 19 August 2026, and the OBR took a later reading, the five working days to 15 September, for its debt interest. It notes the ten-year yield has ranged from about 4.5 to 5.5 per cent since March, a range it calls not unusual by historical standards.

sources.quote: Gilt yields have recently been volatile, with the ten-year yield ranging from around 4.5 per cent to 5.5 per cent since March. But yields within this range are not unusual by historical standards.

considerations.text: Higher rates also raise the interest cost of any extra borrowing you choose (shown as the mechanical debt-interest line). A full OBR forecast would also change growth and inflation in response; this tool does not.
